req.title: Reuse db connection per request
req.statement: The system shall reuse a single sqlite3 connection per Flask request via flask.g.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-025 requires that a single sqlite3 connection is reused per Flask request via flask.g. The violation was test[2] having kind=negative but heuristic=STC. STC (State Transition Coverage) is appropriate for positive or boundary tests that exercise state transitions, not negative tests. The teardown test (close_db removes connection from g) is better classified as kind=positive with heuristic=STC, since it exercises the valid state transition: connection present in g -> close_db() called -> connection absent from g. This is a normal, expected state transition (positive behaviour), not an error pathway. All other tests are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_same_connection_within_request
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary DATABASE path
An application context is active (simulating a single request)
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db() twice within the same context
Compare the two returned connection objects
expected: Both calls return the exact same sqlite3.Connection object (identity check)
The connection is stored in flask.g under key 'db'
trace: R-FLASKR-025: single connection reused per request via flask.g
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_get_db_returns_same_connection_within_request():
    with app.app_context():
        conn1 = get_db()
        conn2 = get_db()
        assert conn1 is conn2, "get_db() must return the same object on repeated calls"
        assert 'db' in g, "connection must be stored in flask.g under key 'db'"
        assert g.db is conn1, "g.db must be identical to the returned connection"

tests.name: test_get_db_returns_different_connection_across_requests
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary DATABASE path
Two separate application contexts are used to simulate two separate requests
actions: Push first application context, call get_db(), record id, pop context
Push second application context, call get_db(), record id, pop context
Compare the two connection object ids
expected: The two connection objects are NOT the same (different ids across requests)
Each context independently stores its own connection in g
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection is per-request, not shared across requests
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_get_db_returns_different_connection_across_requests():
    conn_id_1 = None
    conn_id_2 = None
    with app.app_context():
        conn_id_1 = id(get_db())
    with app.app_context():
        conn_id_2 = id(get_db())
    assert conn_id_1 is not None
    assert conn_id_2 is not None
    assert conn_id_1 != conn_id_2, "Connections across requests must be distinct objects"

tests.name: test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g_after_request
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary DATABASE path
actions: Push an application context
Call get_db() to establish the connection in g (state: db present in g)
Call close_db() explicitly to simulate teardown (state transition: db present -> db absent)
Check that 'db' is no longer present in g
expected: After close_db(), 'db' key is absent from flask.g
close_db() does not raise any exception
State transition from connection-open to connection-closed completes successfully
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection is cleaned up after request via teardown_appcontext
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, close_db, init_db
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_close_db_removes_connection_from_g_after_request():
    with app.app_context():
        conn = get_db()
        assert 'db' in g, "'db' must be in g after get_db() is called"
        assert g.db is conn
        close_db()
        assert 'db' not in g, "'db' must be removed from g after close_db()"

tests.name: test_http_request_succeeds_and_connection_reused_internally
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary DATABASE path
Database initialised with init_db() so schema and seed data exist
actions: Issue GET / via test client (blog index calls get_db() at least once)
Assert HTTP 200 response
Issue GET /hello via test client (no db call, sanity check)
Assert HTTP 200 response
expected: GET / returns HTTP 200 (connection reuse did not break the response)
trace: R-FLASKR-025: expected outcome is HTTP 2xx with expected payload
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_http_request_succeeds_and_connection_reused_internally():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200, got {r.status_code}"
    r2 = client.get('/hello')
    assert r2.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200, got {r2.status_code}"
    assert b'Hello, World!' in r2.data

tests.name: test_close_db_is_idempotent_when_no_connection_exists
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary DATABASE path
An application context is active but get_db() has NOT been called
actions: Push an application context without calling get_db()
Call close_db() directly (g has no 'db' key)
Assert no exception is raised
expected: close_db() returns without raising any exception when g has no 'db'
'db' remains absent from g after the call
trace: R-FLASKR-025: close_db uses g.pop('db', None) — safe when no connection
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import close_db
from flask import g

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

def test_close_db_is_idempotent_when_no_connection_exists():
    with app.app_context():
        assert 'db' not in g, "Precondition: g must not have 'db' before test"
        try:
            close_db()
        except Exception as exc:
            assert False, f"close_db() raised unexpectedly: {exc}"
        assert 'db' not in g, "'db' must still be absent after close_db() with no connection"

tests.name: test_get_db_connection_has_row_factory_set
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temporary DATABASE path
actions: Call get_db() within an app context
Inspect the row_factory attribute of the returned connection
Assert it is sqlite3.Row
expected: The connection is fully configured for dict-like row access
trace: R-FLASKR-025: connection configured correctly when created via get_db()

import tempfile, os, sqlite3
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import get_db, init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_get_db_connection_has_row_factory_set():
    with app.app_context():
        conn = get_db()
        assert conn.row_factory is sqlite3.Row, (
            f"Expected row_factory=sqlite3.Row, got {conn.row_factory}"
        )
